key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO₂ or La₂O₃ to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co reduced porosity and refined grains, with CeO₂ delivering the lowest friction and La₂O₃ the lowest wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide additions offer a route to harder, more wear-resistant WC–12Co coatings without compromising bond strength in the reported tests.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO₂- or La₂O₃-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phase composition, microhardness, bond strength, abrasive wear, and friction.
Examine worn surfaces by SEM to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: At 1 wt.% addition, CeO₂ and La₂O₃ increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively; La₂O₃ achieved a minimum wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while CeO₂ achieved the lowest friction coefficient of 0.4.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or long-term performance, limiting direct extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
